one_line: Pandya king of 8th-century Pandya Nadu, restorer of Brahmadeya land grants like Velvikudi.

appearance.face: oval face with strong jaw, medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp dark eyes under slightly arched brows, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, default expression calm and authoritative with a hint of thoughtful intensity
appearance.hair: thick black hair pulled back into a high, tight kudumi (topknot) at the crown, sides smooth and oiled, with a simple gold circlet crown featuring a small central leaf-shaped ornament resting just above the forehead
appearance.costume: era-accurate Pandya royal attire: a rich deep-maroon silk angavastram wrapped over the left shoulder and across the torso, leaving both shoulders covered in modest overlapping folds, over a fitted pale-cream cotton tunic with half sleeves; lower body in a gold-bordered off-white veshti (dhoti) wrapped to ankle length with a front pleat and broad woven mustard-gold border, secured with a plain gold waist-belt; feet in dark brown leather sandals; jewellery limited to a medium-width gold torque necklace, two simple gold bangles per wrist, and small round gold earrings; a narrow sandalwood-paste tilaka marked vertically on the forehead, and subtle, repeated geometric border patterns on the angavastram’s edges in darker maroon.
appearance.signature: a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a dark green cord, held in his left hand, with the impression of a circular royal seal visible on one end

ref_desc: Jatila Parantaka Nedunjadaiyan is a mid-30s Pandya king with medium-brown skin, high black kudumi and gold circlet, maroon silk angavastram, off-white gold-bordered veshti, modest gold jewellery, brown sandals, and a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a green cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Jatila Parantaka Nedunjadaiyan: a mid-30s Pandya king with medium-brown South Indian complexion, oval face, sharp dark eyes, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, and a calm authoritative expression. His thick black hair is pulled into a high kudumi topknot, smooth at the sides, topped with a simple gold circlet crown that has a small central leaf-shaped ornament above the forehead. Mark a narrow vertical sandalwood-paste tilaka on his forehead. Dress him in 8th-century Pandya royal clothing: a deep-maroon silk angavastram wrapped over the left shoulder and across the torso in modest folds, covering both shoulders; beneath it, a pale-cream cotton tunic with half sleeves; and an off-white veshti (dhoti) reaching the ankles, front-pleated, with a broad mustard-gold woven border. Cinch the waist with a plain gold belt. Put dark brown leather sandals on his feet. Add restrained jewellery: a medium-width gold torque necklace, two simple gold bangles on each wrist, and small round gold earrings. The angavastram’s edges should have subtle darker-maroon geometric border patterns. In his left hand he firmly holds his signature prop, a rolled copper-plate charter tied with a dark green cord, the impression of a circular royal seal visible at one end. Show him in a neutral standing pose that clearly reveals his face, hair, crown, full costume from head to toe, sandals, jewellery, and the copper-plate charter, with clean colors emphasizing deep maroon, off-white, mustard gold, dark brown, and his medium-brown skin.
